research:
I found 10 episode ideas, mapped to this week's order. Dhanteras is 6 Nov and Diwali is Sunday 8 Nov ([Timeout](https://www.timeout.com/india/news/diwali-2026-when-is-dhanteras-diwali-and-bhai-dooj-110226), [Hindutone](https://hindutone.com/festivals/diwali-2026-the-complete-5-day-festival-guide/)). If episodes are made a week ahead, the Diwali ideas only work if they can go out on 6 to 8 Nov.

**Before you use these:** I didn't open the live official pages. Every link below is a government site or a big platform's own page and is free by design, but a quick click-check is still needed before anything goes into `brand/free.json`. I also found nothing on @ashutoshwithclaude or @canwebuildthis (see the last bullet).

1. **REAL FIX · Gemini gives the fix.** Hook: "Rs 8,000 'Diwali bonus'. 1 link." A fake WhatsApp message promises a Rs 8,000 government Diwali bonus and leads to a site that collects your details. PIB called it fake on 2 Nov ([Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/india/story/rs-8000-diwali-bonus-scam-pib-warns-against-fake-whatsapp-messages-claiming-pms-cash-benefit-565151-2026-11-03), [Telangana Today](https://telanganatoday.com/fake-diwali-whatsapp-message-offers-rs-8000-tgcsb-issues-warning)).
   - **The fix:** forward the message to PIB Fact Check on WhatsApp at +91 8799711259 or factcheck@pib.gov.in ([PIB on Telegram](https://t.me/s/PIB_FactCheck/1546)). Report the sender on [Chakshu at sancharsaathi.gov.in](https://www.sancharsaathi.gov.in). If money has gone, call 1930 or use [cybercrime.gov.in](https://cybercrime.gov.in).
   - **The joke:** Gemini's urge to share is the turn: "Done! I sent it to PIB." Keep the wording to "a government bonus" so it stays non-political.

2. **MUM ASKS (the one rebuilt slot).** Hook: "Mum: 'light cut at 9:30 pm tonight'". Fake "your power will be cut tonight" texts push people to call a number or install an app. A 66-year-old lost Rs 1.2 lakh this way ([Tribune](https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/jalandhar/sr-citizen-loses-rs-1-2l-in-electricity-bill-scam-427428)), and Chennai police warned about it in Sept 2026 ([News Today](https://newstodaynet.com/2026/09/18/new-cyber-scam-targets-electricity-consumers/)).
   - **The fix:** never call the number in the message. Check the bill on your electricity board's own app or website, then report the text on [Chakshu](https://www.sancharsaathi.gov.in).
   - **Claude's analogy:** "The bijli office doesn't WhatsApp you, just like the bank manager doesn't come home for your PIN."
   - **Why this one:** 058 already covered voice clones. If you'd rather redo that, the strategy's hook "Mum nearly sent Rs 20,000 to 'me'" fits, and there's a real Rs 97,500 case from Indore ([the420](https://the420.in/ai-voice-cloning-scams-india-how-to-verify-calls/)).

3. **REAL FIX · Codex gives the fix.** Hook: "Rs 4,000 gone. I only tapped 'receive'." The scam is "enter your PIN to receive money", including fake refunds during festive sales ([FPJ](https://www.freepressjournal.in/tech/diwali-2026-8-smartphone-online-shopping-scams-to-watch-out-for-during-festive-sales)).
   - **The fix:** receiving money never needs a PIN. Since Oct 2025, UPI also no longer lets one person send another a "collect" request to approve ([Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/personal-finance/banking/story/npci-to-tighten-upi-rules-peer-to-peer-collect-feature-to-end-in-october-489244-2025-08-13)). So any person asking you to approve a payment request is fake. The official source is [npci.org.in](https://www.npci.org.in).
   - **Codex's honest line:** "Receiving needs no PIN."

4. **AI RUNS MY SHOP · Gemini.** Hook: "Diwali rush: 37 orders. Rs 0 received." Fake "payment done" screenshots and fake QR codes are common in festive sales ([FPJ](https://www.freepressjournal.in/tech/diwali-2026-8-smartphone-online-shopping-scams-to-watch-out-for-during-festive-sales)).
   - **The fix:** a method, no tool needed. Only ship once the money shows in your own bank or UPI app history, never on a screenshot, and keep your own printed QR code.
   - **The gag:** "Orders: 37" on the laptop. Twin: "Paid: 0."

5. **REAL FIX · Claude gives the fix.** Hook: "Offer letter. Rs 2,999 'joining fee'." Job and task scams reach freshers on WhatsApp and Telegram, with offers made without an interview and fees for "training" or "documents" ([Digit](https://www.digit.in/news/general/online-job-scam-alert-scammers-on-whatsapp-and-telegram-targeting-users-with-fake-task-offers.html), [Beincareer](https://beincareer.com/fake-job-offers-warning-signs/)).
   - **The fix:** look the company up free on [mca.gov.in](https://www.mca.gov.in) under MCA Services, "View Company/LLP Master Data". Compare the name, office address and directors with the letter, and check the email domain. One guide says a login is needed for the lookup, so check that. Report at [cybercrime.gov.in](https://cybercrime.gov.in).
   - **The joke:** Claude's caveats are useful for once, but it's still a five-part essay.

6. **AFTER HOURS · PART 1 (the new test) · Gemini.** Hook: "Boss texted at 11:47 pm. 88% of you too." An Indeed survey found 88% of Indian employees get contacted after hours and 79% fear missing promotions if they don't reply ([Staffing Industry](https://www.staffingindustry.com/news/global-daily-news/most-indian-employers-support-right-to-disconnect)). The survey is from about 2025. A Right to Disconnect bill exists but is **not law** ([Vidhi](https://vidhilegalpolicy.in/blog/right-to-disconnect-in-india/)), so don't promise any rights.
   - **The fix:** write your reply now and set it to send at 9:30 am with Gmail or Outlook's built-in "schedule send". Set Do Not Disturb with exceptions for real emergencies. These are standard free features, but I didn't look them up this session.
   - **The joke:** Gemini schedules it, then: "I also told your boss you're asleep."

7. **REAL FIX · Gemini.** Hook: "Average hike: 9.1%. Mine: 'we'll see'." Aon's survey (14 Oct) projects a 9.1% average raise in India for 2027, with attrition up to 18% ([Aon](https://www.aon.com/apac/in-the-press/asia-newsroom/2026/aon-study-finds-salaries-in-india-projected-to-fise-9-1-in-2027-employers-balance-growth-and-cost-pressures)).
   - **The fix:** a method. Make a one-page "wins" list from your own sent emails and calendar, with numbers, and bring the public Aon figure as context. This is career help, not financial advice.
   - **The joke:** Gemini really can pull your year from mail and calendar, which fits it. Claude writes a 6-page self-review first.
   - **Balance:** using Gemini here and in idea 1 gives the experiment 2 Gemini real fixes, against Codex (idea 3) and Claude (idea 5).

8. **REAL FIX (backup) · exams.** Hook: "JEE form closes 22 Nov, 11:50 pm." JEE Main 2027 Session 1 registration closes 22 Nov, with a late window 23 to 26 Nov ([Careers360](https://engineering.careers360.com/articles/jee-main-application-form)). These dates come from a third-party site, so confirm them on [jeemain.nta.nic.in](https://jeemain.nta.nic.in).
   - **The fix:** apply only on the official site, never through a forwarded link, and use an AI checklist for documents.
   - **The joke:** Codex fills in the form for "Meera's cousin" a little too literally.

9. **Dates in the next 10 days:**
   - **Dhanteras 6 Nov, Diwali 8 Nov.** Fake bonus and gift-link warnings are already out from Maharashtra Cyber (4 Nov) ([FPJ](https://www.freepressjournal.in/tech/maharashtra-cyber-police-warn-citizens-against-diwali-message-scams-urge-caution-over-fake-gift-links-online-fraud)).
   - **Bhai Dooj 10 or 11 Nov** and **Chhath around 15 Nov:** sources disagree on both, so don't put either date in a hook.
   - **Just outside the window:** JEE closes 22 Nov, and CAT is 29 Nov with admit cards out since 4 Nov ([Careers360](https://news.careers360.com/cat-admit-card-2026-download-link-iimcat-ac-in-november-4-exam-date-iim-indore-mba-admission-b-school/amp)). The legal deadline for private-sector statutory bonus is 30 Nov, so a bonus that hasn't come by Diwali isn't necessarily late ([HR Tailor](https://hrtailor.com/statutory-bonus-india-2026/)).

10. **A real-life anchor for the AI behaviour:** a Stanford study in *Science* (March 2026) tested 11 AI models and found they backed users' actions 49% more often than people did ([AP via WTOP](https://wtop.com/lifestyle/2026/03/ai-is-giving-bad-advice-to-flatter-its-users-says-new-study-on-dangers-of-overly-agreeable-chatbots/)). That supports the "You're absolutely right!" beat: Meera pushes back wrongly ("it's probably real?") and Claude agrees straight away, before the real fix lands.

11. **Benchmark pages:** web search found nothing on @ashutoshwithclaude or @canwebuildthis this month, only tools and unrelated people. Their current hooks and comment numbers need checking by hand in the Instagram app. I haven't filled that gap with guesses.
